questions.question: Describe how British control of the Gold Coast grew from 1850 to 1874.
questions.expected_answer: Britain became the main European power on the coast when the Danes sold their forts in 1850 and the Dutch handed over theirs, including Elmina, in 1872, giving Britain the whole coastline and growing influence over the Fante. The Asante, who claimed rights at Elmina and used it as an outlet, saw this as a threat and invaded the coast in 1873. General Sir Garnet Wolseley led a carefully planned expedition with a forest road, depots, British, West Indian and African troops and carriers, breech-loading rifles, artillery, rockets and quinine; after fighting at Amoafo the British entered Kumasi in February 1874, burned it and the palace, and withdrew. The Treaty of Fomena required a gold indemnity, renunciation of Elmina and the coastal states, open trade routes and an end to human sacrifice, and Britain declared the Gold Coast Colony in 1874. Some states broke away and civil wars followed, but the kingdom survived and Prempeh became Asantehene in 1888.

questions.question: Explain why and how Britain took control of Asante in 1896.
questions.expected_answer: During the scramble France was expanding from the west and north and Germany held Togoland from 1884, so British officials and merchants feared losing Asante and the north, and wanted direct access to gold, rubber, timber and northern markets. Prempeh I refused a treaty of protection in 1891, saying Asante wished to be friendly with all but subject to none, and sent envoys to London in 1894 to 1895, who were not officially received. In late 1895 Britain sent an expedition, citing the unpaid 1874 indemnity, closed trade routes and human sacrifice. Prempeh chose not to fight to avoid his people's destruction; in January 1896 the British entered Kumasi unopposed, forced him to submit humiliatingly and promise a huge gold payment, and arrested him, the queen mother and leading chiefs. He was exiled to Elmina, Sierra Leone and in 1900 the Seychelles, Asante became a protectorate with a British Resident and fort, and the British searched for the Golden Stool.

questions.question: Describe the War of the Golden Stool and its outcome.
questions.expected_answer: In March 1900 Governor Hodgson demanded the indemnity and asked where the Golden Stool was, saying he should sit on it, a profound insult because the stool held the nation's spirit and no one sat on it. According to tradition, Yaa Asantewaa, queen mother of Ejisu, challenged the chiefs, saying the women would fight if the men would not, and became war leader. From late March the Asante besieged the British fort in Kumasi, cut telegraph lines and blocked roads with stockades; people in the fort suffered hunger and disease, Hodgson broke out in June and a relief force lifted the siege in July. British forces, including many African soldiers, won a series of battles and burned villages; Yaa Asantewaa was captured in 1901 and exiled to the Seychelles, dying there in 1921. Asante was annexed as a colony from 1 January 1902 and the Northern Territories became a protectorate. The British never captured the Golden Stool, which was hidden for twenty years and remains a symbol of the Asante nation.
